text: Before comparing two models on perplexity, watch what happens to the exact same sentence under two tokenizers. The words stay put; only the cuts move. Hold the total surprise fixed and split the passage into more pieces. The per-token average falls, even though the score for the text as a whole hasn't changed. Count bits, divide by the raw UTF-eight bytes, and you have bits per byte. Same text, same denominator. The models can still give it different probabilities. For a long time, language modeling benchmarks asked you to train and test on splits of the same corpus, like Penn Treebank or WikiText one oh three. GPT-two took a different route: pretrain on broad web text, then measure zero-shot perplexity on those benchmark corpora, without fitting a model to each one.

direction: Warm adult American English male speaking to a few students, not projecting into a hall. Begin conversationally, and let an unexpected fact change the voice naturally: brief curiosity, then a lucid explanation. Use distinct logical stresses and connected sentences. Maintain an easy, measured teaching pace, brisk but unhurried. Keep momentum through sentences with ordinary breathing room around the main question; about 165 words per minute. Thoughtful rather than an announcer. Pronounce the encoding name as the four distinct sounds you, tee, eff, eight. Continue at an active natural pace; lightly stress only the cuts move and same denominator, with short connected pauses.
